meta.title: MAU +20% QoQ, revenue flat: what is happening and what to do
meta.short_title: MAU up, revenue flat (Q3 vs Q2 2026)
meta.question: MAU is up 20% QoQ but revenue is flat. Board meeting Thursday. Figure out what's happening and what we should do about it.
meta.mode: Independent (no answer keys, guides or generator README read)
meta.periods: Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) vs Q2 2026 (Apr-Jun), UTC calendar months
meta.author: Claude Code (Opus 5.5) with the shared investigation skill

items: Check N = one logged read-only query. Each logs/qNN.jsonl holds its SQL, parameters, layer, version, limitations and rows (inputs in requests/qNN.json). No query was truncated or failed.
Data layers: Gold = pre-built monthly summary tables, Silver = cleaned detail tables, Bronze = raw source records.
Quarter figures: quarter MAU is the average of its three monthly MAUs; quarter revenue is the sum of its three months.
Patterns, not proof: the data is observational and synthetic. Where the report says a pattern is 'associated with' something, the cause has not been proven.
MAU (v1.1)
Distinct identified users with at least one session overlapping the UTC month. Logged-out sessions with no same-session login are excluded.
Net revenue (v1.1)
Successful subscription and PPV charges minus successful refunds, booked when the payment succeeds. Net of refunds only (no fees or tax data).
Paying users
Users with at least one successful subscription or PPV charge in the month.
Paywall-exposed users
Distinct identified users who saw at least one paywall in the month (paywall_exposure).
30-day paywall reach
Share of a signup cohort that saw a paywall within 30 days of signup (ad hoc, built on registered cohort rules).
Acquisition source
The user's fixed first-touch channel: organic, paid search, paid social or unknown.

blocks.text: The premise holds: average MAU rose 20.0% while net revenue rose 0.07%. The extra users, mostly paid-social signups, are not reaching the paywall. About 1,000 people see a paywall each month, so the paying base stays at about 1,000 subscribers on a $9.99 plan.

items: Where the growth came from: paid-social MAU rose by 1,841 a month on average, more than the total gain of 1,803. Paid-social spend rose 121% (checks 5, 7).
Why revenue stayed flat: 99.3% of revenue is subscriptions. About 100 subscribers lapse each month and about 100 join, so the base stays at about 1,000 (checks 2, 17).

Where the path breaks: paywall viewers stayed at about 1,000 a month while MAU grew. 30-day paywall reach for new signups fell from 4.4% (May) to 0.5% (August). Conversion after the paywall did not get worse (checks 8, 13).
Cost: Q3 paid social cost $30,760 and brought 67 new paying users, about $459 each (check 7).

blocks.title: Recommendation in one line:
blocks.text: Tell the board that the MAU growth is paid reach that has not monetised yet. Cap further paid-social scale-up until a payback check passes. Make getting new users to their first paywall the Q4 priority.

rows: Q2 = Apr-Jun 2026, Q3 = Jul-Sep 2026; complete UTC months, half-open.
mau 1.1, revenue 1.1, growth accounting 1.0, funnel and lifecycle 1.0, engagement 1.0, supporting 1.1 (from the build log, check 1). Slices by source and cohort are labelled ad hoc.

items: Paid social spend: $13,918 in Q2 and $30,760 in Q3 (+121%). Paid-social signups went from 1,489 to 4,568 (check 7). Spend ramped in July, the same month paid-social MAU jumped from 2,299 to 3,358 (check 5). The timing matches, but this does not prove the spend caused the growth: there is no click-level attribution.

Growth accounting: retained users stayed at about 4,400-5,070 a month. Growth came from new signups (1,720-2,949 a month) and returning users (2,176 rising to 4,656), while churned users rose from 3,180 to 5,800 (check 3).

The old base is shrinking and still carries revenue: users who signed up before April fell from 6,337 to 4,659 active, and their payers from 1,019 to 693. Payers from Q2 signups (303 a month in Q3) only replaced that loss. Q3 signups had 54 payers by September (check 14).

rows: Growth is from a low-monetising channel
Paid social is 102% of the net MAU gain. Its exposure rate fell from 10-12% (Q2) to 6.1-6.9% (Q3), while other sources stayed at 9.5-12.4% (checks 5, 10).
Revenue capped by a flat subscriber base
977-1,023 subscribers at every month-end; about 100 churn a month and are replaced by about 100 new subscribers (check 2).
Q3 paid-social users watched 28.5-31 minutes a month, against 32-34 for others; 57-59% were engaged, against 59-62% (check 11). The gap is small.
Paywall-to-purchase rate was 9.9-14.7% from May to September, alternating month to month with no trend (check 8).
About 1,000 paywall viewers every month; new-cohort 30-day reach fell from 4.4% to 0.5% in all channels (checks 8, 13).
ARPPU $9.68-9.74; PPV about $69 a month; refunds of $2-14 a month (checks 2, 4).
About 200 blocked plays a month against 1,000+ paywall views, so most paywall triggers are not recorded. Free-quota hit rate fell from 0.84% to 0.68% (checks 9, 12).
One episode tier change in July; subscriber views flat at about 7,000-7,500 a month (check 15).
Layers reconciled; exceptions limited to 13 reviewed payment corrections (checks 1, 16).

blocks.title: Not yet known:
blocks.text: Why new users increasingly fail to reach a paywall in their first 30 days. The data has no in-app navigation or recommendation events, so the cause cannot be identified from this data. It needs instrumentation or an experiment.

rows: Subscription start-up in April 2026 (0 subscribers at 1 April)
Inflates April paywall views, purchases and first payments. Funnel and cohort trends are read from May. Headline conclusions hold without April (MAU +13.2%, revenue -0.8%).
Logged-out sessions: 6.5% (Apr) to 7.6% (Sep) of sessions have no identified user
Excluded from MAU by definition, and they grew roughly in line with sessions. Counting them would only add reach that also does not pay, so the conclusion does not change.
13 raw payment amounts corrected on review
Curated amounts are already used in revenue. These are the only Silver exceptions (check 16).
Purchase attribution only through captured links (about 5% of checkouts unlinked)
Funnel rates are slightly understated; in-app purchases without a checkout link are 1-7 a month (check 8).
One unidentified session spans the Aug/Sep boundary (3,703 in Gold vs 3,702 by start month)
Immaterial. Noted because the registry says no fixture session crosses a month boundary.

items: Synthetic, observational data. The channel, timing and funnel patterns are associations. The report does not claim that paid-social spend caused the MAU growth, or that low paywall reach is the only reason revenue stayed flat.
No lifetime value or payback: the registry marks LTV as unsupported (six months of history), so the $459 per new payer is a monthly ratio of spend to first-time payers, not a cohort payback.
Paywall triggers are only partly recorded (blocked plays). Exposure-by-source and cohort paywall reach are ad hoc slices, with their SQL logged.
Revenue is net of refunds only; app-store fees and tax are not in the data.
Q3 cohorts are young: July-September signups may still monetise. Q2 signups reached 303 payers by Q3, so re-check Q3 cohorts in Q4.
Reframe the board story. Present Q3 as paid reach that has not yet monetised. Report subscribers, paywall-exposed users and new payers next to MAU.

Cap paid-social at its July run-rate (about $10k a month) until incrementality and payback are measured, with a geo or time-based holdout. Check: new payers per $1k of paid-social spend (May-Jun 6.7; Q3 2.2).

Make reaching the first paywall the Q4 product priority for new users. A/B test earlier premium sampling or paywall prompts in week one, and the 8-a-day free quota, which fewer than 1% of free-viewer days reach. Check: 30-day paywall reach and subscription conversion by signup month (both 0.5% for August signups).
Instrument paywall triggers and content navigation, so the fall in paywall reach can be explained, not only observed. Check: every paywall view has a recorded trigger.
Protect the subscriber base. About 100 subscribers (9-11%) lapse each month. Test retention offers. Check: monthly churn rate and month-end subscribers.
Re-run this analysis after October and November close. Confirm whether Q3 cohorts convert with tenure, as Q2 cohorts did.
